README.md.overview: Project entry document for FuelTrack: a Fuelio-inspired multi-vehicle fuel tracker for iPhone built with SwiftUI, SwiftData, and xtool deployment. Tour step 1 points here first so you learn the v1 feature set, Sources/FuelTrack folder map, and how to build, import Fuelio CSV, and run smoke scripts before diving into models and views.

sections.title: Product pitch
sections.explanation: The title and opening sentence frame FuelTrack as a Fuelio-inspired multi-vehicle fuel tracker for iPhone. SwiftUI + SwiftData name the UI and persistence stack; xtool is the deployment path instead of a traditional Xcode `.xcodeproj`. Keep this mental model as you read Package.swift and the app entry later.

sections.title: v1 feature checklist
sections.explanation: The feature list is the product contract for this tour: multiple vehicles, fill-up logging with full/partial and missed flags, GBP/INR and miles/km, full-tank dashboard stats, Fuelio CSV import, custom icon, and on-device-only storage. When you hit Vehicle, FillUp, FuelStats, and import services later, map each back to one of these bullets.

sections.title: Source folder map
sections.explanation: The layout tree shows how the Swift package sources are organized: Models for entities and enums, Services for stats and formatters, Support for active-vehicle state, and Views for feature screens. Use this as a navigation cheat sheet when tour steps jump between layers.

sections.title: Tooling requirements
sections.explanation: Running on a real iPhone needs full Xcode (for the iOS SDK), the xtool CLI, and Developer Mode on the device. The optional `xcodes` install path shows how to pin an Xcode version; without Xcode, `xtool dev` cannot finish even if sources and the CLI are present.

sections.title: First-time setup
sections.explanation: The setup script selects the Xcode developer directory, accepts the license, verifies the iPhone SDK, runs `xtool setup`, then `xtool devices` / `xtool dev` to install on a connected phone. Bundle ID `com.ajaybali.FuelTrack` matches `xtool.yml`, which you meet in tour step 2.

sections.title: Import and verify
sections.explanation: Fuelio import is a three-step migration path; currency must be chosen in FuelTrack because Fuelio CSV omits it. The smoke scripts let you validate FuelStats and CSV parsing without a device. The closing status notes document scaffold readiness and the remaining Xcode/`xtool auth` blockers on the author's machine.

Package.swift.overview: Swift Package Manager manifest that names the FuelTrack library target and declares iOS 26+ and macOS 15+ platforms. Tour step 2 pairs this with xtool.yml: SPM compiles the Sources/FuelTrack code as a library, while xtool layers app packaging metadata on top so the same target becomes a deployable iPhone app without an Xcode project file.

sections.title: Tools version import
sections.explanation: The `swift-tools-version: 6.2` header tells SwiftPM which manifest language and toolchain features are required. Importing `PackageDescription` gives access to the `Package` type used below.

sections.title: Platforms and product
sections.explanation: The package is named FuelTrack and supports iOS 26 and macOS 15. Exposing a `.library` product named FuelTrack that depends on the FuelTrack target is the SPM pattern xtool expects: compile as a library, then wrap it as an app at deploy time.

sections.title: Library target
sections.explanation: A single `.target(name: "FuelTrack")` with no explicit path or dependencies defaults to `Sources/FuelTrack`. There are no external packages here—the app is self-contained SwiftUI/SwiftData code under that folder.

xtool.yml.overview: xtool packaging config that turns the SPM FuelTrack library into a signed iOS app. Tour step 2 covers this alongside Package.swift: bundle ID, app icon, and Info.plist paths are the app-specific metadata SPM does not provide.

sections.title: App packaging metadata
sections.explanation: `version: 1` is the xtool config schema. `bundleID` must match what the README documents (`com.ajaybali.FuelTrack`). `iconPath` and `infoPath` point at the custom icon asset and Info.plist used when `xtool dev` builds, signs, and installs on a phone.

Sources/FuelTrack/FuelTrackApp.swift.overview: SwiftUI `@main` app entry and runtime wiring hub for tour step 3. It registers every SwiftData `@Model` in a shared ModelContainer, then injects ActiveVehicleStore, LocationProvider, and TripRecorder into ContentView so the rest of the app shares one persistence graph and one set of live services.

sections.title: Shared service instances
sections.explanation: After importing SwiftData and SwiftUI, FuelTrackApp is marked `@main` and conforms to `App`. Three long-lived objects—active vehicle store, location provider, and trip recorder—are created once on the app struct so every scene shares the same instances rather than recreating them per view.

sections.title: ModelContainer schema
sections.explanation: The lazy `sharedModelContainer` builds a Schema listing every persistent type: vehicles, fill-ups, costs, reminders, personal finance, stations, and trips. Configuration uses on-disk storage (`isStoredInMemoryOnly: false`). If container creation fails, the store file is deleted and creation is retried once—useful after schema migrations break an old store—before `fatalError` as a last resort.

sections.title: Scene and environment
sections.explanation: `WindowGroup` mounts ContentView and injects the three services via `.environment(...)`. `.modelContainer(sharedModelContainer)` attaches SwiftData to the scene so `@Query` and `@Environment(\.modelContext)` work in descendant views. Everything later in the tour hangs off this bootstrap.

Sources/FuelTrack/Models/FillUp.swift.overview: SwiftData `@Model` for a single fuel purchase: litres, cost, tank fullness, station geodata, and fuel type tied to a Vehicle. Tour step 4 presents FillUp with Vehicle as the core vocabulary for logging fuel and computing economy; FuelStats later segments these rows using the full-tank method.

sections.title: Stored fill-up fields
sections.explanation: FillUp stores odometer, liters, totalCost, tank flags (`isFullTank`, `skipped`), station text, notes, optional coordinates, and an external station id. Currency and fuel type are persisted as raw strings (`currencyCodeRaw`, `fuelTypeRaw`) so SwiftData stores simple scalars while typed accessors wrap them. The optional `vehicle` link is the inverse of Vehicle.fillUps.

sections.title: Initializer defaults
sections.explanation: The initializer accepts typed `CurrencyCode` and optional `FuelType`, then writes their `rawValue`s into storage. Defaults favor a full tank, GBP, and empty station fields so quick logging stays short while still allowing Fuelio import and map flows to fill geodata and external ids.

sections.title: Typed accessors and price
sections.explanation: `currencyCode` falls back to GBP if the raw string is unknown. `fuelType` inherits the vehicle's type when the stored string is empty, maps legacy values through `FuelType.fromStored`, and coerces bare `.petrol` writes to `.petrolE10`. `pricePerLiter` is derived (cost ÷ liters) and returns nil when liters is zero so callers never divide by zero.

Sources/FuelTrack/Models/Vehicle.swift.overview: Hub SwiftData entity for a car: identity, unit/currency preferences, UK DVLA compliance fields, and cascade relationships to fill-ups, costs, reminders, stations, and trips. Tour step 4 introduces Vehicle as the center of the data graph that FillUp and later spend/trip features hang from.

sections.title: Identity and DVLA fields
sections.explanation: Core identity includes name, make, model, and raw-string preferences for fuel type, odometer unit, and currency. The UK compliance block stores registration, colour, engine/CO₂ data, MOT/tax status and dates, insurance, and a last-refresh timestamp—feeding dashboard compliance cards and notification scheduling.

sections.title: Cascade relationships
sections.explanation: Each `@Relationship` uses `.cascade` delete and names the inverse on the child model. Deleting a vehicle therefore removes its fill-ups, costs, reminders, saved stations, and trips, keeping the SwiftData graph consistent without manual orphan cleanup.

sections.title: Init and typed preferences
sections.explanation: Construction defaults to petrol E10, miles, and GBP. Registration is cleaned through `DVLAVehicleService.cleanedRegistration` before storage. Computed `fuelType`, `odometerUnit`, and `currencyCode` wrap the raw fields with safe fallbacks; writing `.petrol` is normalized to `.petrolE10` for forward compatibility.

sections.title: Display and sorted collections
sections.explanation: `displayPlate` inserts a space before the last three characters of a cleaned UK plate. `displaySubtitle` builds a make/model/plate line for list and dashboard headers. Sorted helpers order trips (completed newest-first), fill-ups (odometer then date), costs (newest first), and incomplete reminders by due date—ready for UI without ad-hoc sorting in every view.

sections.title: Spend and compliance helpers
sections.explanation: Month/year/all-time cost totals and `totalCarSpend*` combine car costs with FuelStats fuel spend. `motIsValid` / `taxIsValid` parse DVLA status strings. `applyDVLA` merges API details into the vehicle and maps fuel strings onto FuelType cases. `daysUntil` supports countdown UI for MOT, tax, and insurance dates.

Sources/FuelTrack/Models/CurrencyCode.sw.overview: Constrained currency enum limited to GBP and INR with display names, symbols, and locale identifiers. Tour step 5 groups this with OdometerUnit and FuelType so vehicles and fill-ups share a small, explicit set of domain values used by formatting and import flows.

sections.title: Cases and identity
sections.explanation: `CurrencyCode` is a String-backed enum with only GBP and INR—matching the README v1 scope. Conformance to `CaseIterable`, `Codable`, `Identifiable`, and `Sendable` makes it usable in pickers, persistence, and concurrency-safe APIs. `id` is the ISO currency code string.

sections.title: Display and locale
sections.explanation: `displayName` includes the currency symbol for picker labels; `symbol` is the short glyph used in UI. `localeIdentifier` maps to `en_GB` / `en_IN` so Formatters can produce culturally correct number layouts when presenting amounts for each vehicle or fill-up.

Sources/FuelTrack/Models/FuelType.swift.overview: Fuel grade enum spanning UK petrol blends, diesel, LPG, electric, hybrid, and a legacy `petrol` case. Tour step 5 highlights how these values drive display names, nearby-price API codes, and Fuelio tank codes so import, export, and station pricing stay aligned.

sections.title: Cases and selection
sections.explanation: Modern grades are listed explicitly; `petrol` is retained only for older stored values. `selectableCases` hides that legacy case from pickers. `fromStored` maps raw `"petrol"` to `.petrolE10` and unknown strings to `.other`, so reading old data never crashes on a missing case.

sections.title: Display names
sections.explanation: `displayName` and `shortName` give long labels for forms and compact chips for dense UI. Legacy `.petrol` shares E10 naming so users never see an obsolete "Petrol" grade after migration.

sections.title: API and Fuelio codes
sections.explanation: `nearbyAPIFuelCode` maps supported liquid fuels to UK Fuel Finder codes (E10, E5, B7); other types return nil and `supportsNearbyPrices` gates the stations feature. `fuelioTankCode` chooses Fuelio tank integers so a FuelTrack export re-imports as the same grade—critical for CSV round-trips later in the tour.

Sources/FuelTrack/Models/OdometerUnit.sw.overview: Miles vs kilometres enum with short labels and bidirectional conversion to kilometres. Tour step 5 places it with the other domain enums; dashboard and FuelStats use these conversions so economy math stays consistent regardless of each vehicle's preferred unit.

sections.title: Unit cases and labels
sections.explanation: Two cases cover the README promise of miles or kilometres per vehicle. `shortLabel` (`mi` / `km`) suits chips and odometer rows; `displayName` suits settings pickers. Same protocol mix as CurrencyCode for pickers and Codable storage.

sections.title: Kilometre conversion
sections.explanation: `toKilometers` and `fromKilometers` use the exact 1.609344 factor. Stats engines typically normalize distances to kilometres internally (for L/100km) then convert back with `fromKilometers` when presenting in the vehicle's unit—avoid mixing mi and km in a single formula.

Sources/FuelTrack/Theme/GlassTheme.swift.overview: Visual system for tour step 6: accent colors, appearance preference, full-bleed backdrop, glass cards/chips, and screen transition helpers. DashboardView and ContentView rely on these tokens so Home and the tab shell share one look without per-screen styling.

sections.title: Color tokens
sections.explanation: `GlassTheme` defines the cool accent, warm accent, and deep/ink backgrounds as static Colors. Reusing these constants keeps chips, tints, and trip/compliance highlights consistent across the glass UI.

sections.title: Appearance preference
sections.explanation: `AppearancePreference` maps system/light/dark to an optional `ColorScheme`. ContentView stores the raw value in `@AppStorage` and applies `.preferredColorScheme`, so Settings can override appearance without hard-coding theme logic in every tab.

sections.title: App backdrop
sections.explanation: `AppBackdrop` paints a scheme-aware diagonal gradient plus two blurred accent circles that ignore the safe area. Opacity and gradient stops flip for dark mode, and a smooth animation runs when `colorScheme` changes—giving screens atmosphere without per-view backgrounds.

sections.title: Glass card and chip
sections.explanation: `GlassCard` wraps arbitrary content with padding and iOS glass effect in a 24pt rounded rect—the standard dashboard section container. `GlassStatChip` is a titled value cell with a tint underline, used in the Home grid for L/100km, MPG, and spend figures.

sections.title: Screen transitions
sections.explanation: `SmoothPageAppear` fades/slides content in once and deliberately does not reset on disappear—because NavigationStack keeps parents alive and resetting opacity caused a black screen on back navigation. `fuelTrackScreen()` and `smoothContentTransition()` are the View helpers Dashboard and other tabs call for consistent chrome and motion.

Sources/FuelTrack/Views/ContentView.swif.overview: Root tab shell for tour step 6: Home, Fuel, Spend, Stations, and More. It resolves the active vehicle, applies appearance and glass tint, and reschedules MOT/tax/insurance compliance notifications whenever vehicles or their compliance fields change.

sections.title: Tab enum and state
sections.explanation: `AppTab` enumerates the five top-level destinations. ContentView queries all vehicles, reads ActiveVehicleStore from the environment (injected in FuelTrackApp), restores appearance from `@AppStorage`, and tracks `selectedTab` for the TabView selection binding.

sections.title: TabView shell
sections.explanation: Each tab hosts a feature root: DashboardView (Home), FillUpListView, SpendRootView, NearbyStationsView, and MoreView. GlassTheme accent tints the selected tab; preferred color scheme and smooth animations respond to tab and appearance changes; sensory feedback fires on tab selection.

sections.title: Active vehicle and alerts
sections.explanation: On appear and when the vehicle id list changes, `activeVehicleStore.resolve` picks a valid active vehicle and ComplianceNotificationScheduler rebuilds local alerts. `complianceSignature` concatenates MOT/tax/insurance dates and reminder state so date-only edits also trigger reschedule without requiring a vehicle list change.

Sources/FuelTrack/Views/Dashboard/Dashbo.overview: Home tab root from tour step 6. It resolves the active vehicle, offers an empty/select-vehicle empty state, and composes trip, compliance, fuel quick-access, spend, economy chips, totals, and upcoming reminders—styled with GlassTheme and driven by FuelStats.

sections.title: Active vehicle resolution
sections.explanation: A `@Query` loads vehicles sorted by creation date. `activeVehicle` always goes through `ActiveVehicleStore.resolve`, so Home stays in sync with the same selection ContentView and other tabs use.

sections.title: Empty states and toolbar
sections.explanation: Inside a NavigationStack, the view branches: no vehicles → prompt to add one; resolved vehicle → dashboard; otherwise → prompt to pick a vehicle in More. The trailing menu lists every vehicle and marks the active one with a checkmark via `activeVehicleStore.select`. `.fuelTrackScreen()` applies the glass backdrop and appear animation.

sections.title: Dashboard card stack
sections.explanation: `vehicleDashboard` computes FuelStats once, then stacks GlassCards and feature cards: identity/odometer header, HomeTripCard, optional VehicleComplianceCard, fuel quick access, car and personal spend cards, a 2×2 GlassStatChip grid for economy and monthly spend, then detailed fuel-economy and totals cards. Open reminders show up to three upcoming items. This composition is the main consumer of the models and theme from earlier tour steps.

sections.title: Label-value row helper
sections.explanation: A small private `row` helper renders secondary label + medium-weight value pairs used inside the economy and totals cards, keeping those sections visually consistent without repeating HStack boilerplate.

Sources/FuelTrack/Services/Formatters.sw.overview: Formatters is a small static utility that turns raw fuel, money, and trip numbers into consistent UI strings. Tour step 7 pairs it with FuelStats: the stats engine computes values, and this file decides how currency, L/100km, MPG, odometer, and trip duration appear on dashboard and fill-up cards. Every display path that needs locale-aware currency or unit labels funnels through these helpers.

sections.title: Currency and volume
sections.explanation: The enum groups pure formatting functions with no shared state. `currency` builds a `NumberFormatter` using the vehicle’s `CurrencyCode` so GBP and INR pick the right locale and symbol, with a simple fallback if formatting fails. `liters` always appends an `L` suffix at two decimal places so volume reads the same across the Fuel tab and stats chips.

sections.title: Economy and unit labels
sections.explanation: Odometer, L/100km, MPG, cost-per-distance, and price-per-litre helpers all accept optional values and render an em dash when data is missing—important because FuelStats often returns `nil` until a full-tank segment exists. Cost and price helpers reuse `currency` so the same locale rules apply whether the UI shows spend totals or per-litre rates.

sections.title: Dates and trip metrics
sections.explanation: `shortDate` uses Swift’s built-in abbreviated date style for fill-up cards and favourites. Trip helpers format speed and distance with the vehicle’s odometer unit, while `tripDuration` converts seconds into `m:ss` or `h:mm:ss` so the live trip UI stays readable without pulling in DateComponentsFormatter.

Sources/FuelTrack/Services/FuelStats.swi.overview: FuelStats implements the full-tank consumption method described in the README and tour step 7. It defines lightweight snapshots and segments so math can run without SwiftData objects, then aggregates spend, economy, and period totals for the dashboard. Understanding this file explains why partial fills and “missed fill-up” flags matter for MPG.

sections.title: Snapshot and segment types
sections.explanation: `FillUpSnapshot` is a Sendable value copy of the fields needed for economy math, keeping the service free of SwiftData. `ConsumptionSegment` stores the odometer span plus liters and cost between two full tanks, and derives distance, L/100km (after converting the vehicle’s unit to kilometres), UK imperial MPG via the 282.481 constant, and cost per distance.

sections.title: VehicleFuelStats bag
sections.explanation: `VehicleFuelStats` is the single result type the UI consumes: counts, totals, averages, month/year spend, the last segment, and the full segment list. Keeping everything in one struct lets Dashboard and HomeTripCard call `FuelStats.compute` once and pick the fields they need.

sections.title: Full-tank segment builder
sections.explanation: `segments(from:)` sorts by odometer then date, then walks fill-ups looking for full tanks. Each new full tank closes a segment from the previous full tank, summing liters and cost for every fill in between (including partials). A `skipped` row clears `startIndex`, breaking the chain so a missed fill-up does not invent false economy.

sections.title: Aggregate compute APIs
sections.explanation: `compute(fillUps:unit:…)` builds segments, totals liters/spend, averages price per liter across priced fills, and weights L/100km and MPG across all segment distance. Month and year spend use the injected calendar and `now` for testability. The Vehicle overload maps SwiftData fill-ups into snapshots so views never duplicate that conversion.

Sources/FuelTrack/Views/FillUps/FillUpFo.overview: FillUpFormView is the create/edit sheet for a single fill-up in tour step 8’s logging flow. It binds form fields to local state, validates numeric input, optionally pulls station and price data from StationPickerView, and inserts or updates a SwiftData `FillUp` on the active vehicle. New fills default currency, fuel type, and odometer from the vehicle.

sections.title: State and validation
sections.explanation: The view takes a required `Vehicle` and an optional existing `FillUp` to distinguish add vs edit. Text fields store odometer, liters, and cost as strings so the decimal pad works with both comma and period; computed parsers and `canSave` gate the Save button until values are non-negative and liters are positive.

sections.title: Form sections and preview
sections.explanation: The body is a Form with Fill-up, Tank, Details, and optional Preview sections. Tank toggles map directly to full-tank and skipped flags used by FuelStats. The station row opens StationPickerView; when a nearby price exists in GBP, the form can prefill or fill total cost from pence-per-litre. Toolbar Save/Cancel and `onAppear(load)` complete the sheet lifecycle.

sections.title: Station apply and load
sections.explanation: `applyStation` treats synthetic `used-` picks as name-only (no geodata), while real nearby stations compose a brand · name · city · postcode label and store coordinates plus listed price. `load` hydrates fields when editing, or seeds currency, fuel type, and the latest odometer for new entries so logging stays fast.

sections.title: Persist fill-up
sections.explanation: `save` either mutates the existing model or inserts a new `FillUp` linked to the vehicle, trimming station and note whitespace. A successful `modelContext.save` triggers haptic success and dismisses; failures surface `saveError` and an error haptic so the user can correct input without losing the sheet.

Sources/FuelTrack/Views/FillUps/FillUpLi.overview: FillUpListView is the Fuel tab list from tour step 8: it resolves the active vehicle, shows month spend/volume summary, and lists fill-ups as glass cards with edit navigation and delete. Empty states guide users who have no vehicle or no fills yet. The private FillUpCard presents date, station, cost, and tank badges using Formatters.

sections.title: Active vehicle and month totals
sections.explanation: A `@Query` loads vehicles while `ActiveVehicleStore` picks which one’s fill-ups to show. Fill-ups come from `sortedFillUps.reversed()` for newest-first. Month spend and liters filter by calendar month start so the summary matches FuelStats’ period idea without recomputing full economy here.

sections.title: List, toolbar, and add sheet
sections.explanation: The NavigationStack switches between ContentUnavailableView empty states and a ScrollView of NavigationLinks into FillUpFormView. Context menus delete fills immediately. The leading menu switches vehicles; trailing controls open the fill-up map and present the add sheet only when an active vehicle exists.

sections.title: Month summary card
sections.explanation: `summary(for:)` uses GlassCard and GlassStatChip to show this month’s currency total, liters, fill count, lifetime fill count, and last-fill date. That gives the Fuel tab a dashboard-like header before the chronological list.

sections.title: FillUpCard presentation
sections.explanation: FillUpCard is a private glass row: date and station (or fuel type) on the left, total cost on the right, then volume/odometer/price metrics. Capsules and colored captions communicate fuel type, full vs partial tank, and “Missed prior” when `skipped` is set—the same flags FuelStats relies on.

Sources/FuelTrack/Views/FillUps/StationP.overview: StationPickerView, also in tour step 8, lets the user pick a station from past favourites or live nearby prices. It merges UsedStations summaries with NearbyStationsService results, supports search and cheapest/nearest sort, and waits briefly for GPS before fetching. Callbacks return either a full NearbyStation or a name-only favourite.

sections.title: Callbacks and filtered lists
sections.explanation: The initializer stores `onSelectNearby` and optional `onSelectName`. Favourites come from fill-up history via `UsedStations.favourites`; nearby stations live in `@State` and are filtered by search, then sorted by price or distance depending on `sortCheapest`. Missing prices/distances sort last via `greatestFiniteMagnitude`.

sections.title: Picker UI and controls
sections.explanation: Loading, error, and empty ContentUnavailableView states cover GPS and API failures. The list shows a Favourites section then Nearby rows, with searchable text and a menu for radius (10/20/30 mi), sort mode, and refresh. `.task` and radius `onChange` both call `load` so widening the search refetches automatically.

sections.title: Row views and selectUsed
sections.explanation: `usedRow` and `nearbyRow` show name, visit/price/distance metadata, and a plus affordance. `selectUsed` prefers a live nearby match for current price and coordinates; otherwise it calls `onSelectName` or synthesizes a `used-` NearbyStation with a zero coordinate—the same convention FillUpFormView’s `applyStation` understands.

sections.title: Location-aware load
sections.explanation: `load` maps the form’s fuel type to a nearby API code, requests location if needed, and polls up to about 2.4 seconds for a fix because the sheet often opens before GPS settles. It then fetches up to 100 stations within `radiusMiles` and surfaces empty-radius or network errors without wiping favourites.

Sources/FuelTrack/Models/Trip.swift.overview: Trip is the SwiftData model for a GPS journey in tour step 9. It stores timing, distance, speed, estimated economy from fuel averages, start/end coordinates, and a cascade relationship to ordered TripPoints. Status is stored as a raw string for persistence while a computed property exposes the typed TripStatus enum.

sections.title: Persisted trip fields
sections.explanation: The `@Model` declares identity, start/end times, status raw value, path metrics, optional economy estimates, endpoints, note, timestamps, an optional Vehicle link, and a cascade `points` relationship. Cascading deletes keep TripPoint rows from orphaning when a trip is discarded or emptied.

sections.title: Initializer and accessors
sections.explanation: The initializer defaults to an active trip with zero metrics and empty points, converting `TripStatus` into `statusRaw`. The `status` computed property round-trips the enum (falling back to `.completed` if the raw value is unknown). `sortedPoints` orders by `sequence` so the recorder and UI can replay the path regardless of how SwiftData returns the unordered relationship.

Sources/FuelTrack/Models/TripPoint.swift.overview: TripPoint is the GPS sample model for tour step 9’s trip logger. Each row records a timestamped coordinate, optional speed and horizontal accuracy, and a monotonic sequence within its parent Trip. TripRecorder inserts these as Core Location delivers updates.

sections.title: Point model and init
sections.explanation: As a SwiftData `@Model`, TripPoint keeps only what the path needs: lat/lon, optional speed in m/s, accuracy, and sequence. The optional `trip` inverse completes the relationship declared on Trip. Sequence—not timestamp alone—is the authoritative path order when points are sorted for distance reconstruction and end-coordinate selection.

Sources/FuelTrack/Services/TripRecorder..overview: TripRecorder is the observable Core Location service at the heart of tour step 9. It starts and ends SwiftData trips, appends TripPoints, filters bad GPS jumps, and publishes live distance/speed/economy for HomeTripCard and ActiveTripView. It also restores an in-progress trip after relaunch and upgrades When-In-Use toward Always when possible.

sections.title: Observable session state
sections.explanation: Marked `@MainActor` and `@Observable`, the recorder owns a CLLocationManager configured for best accuracy and a 10 m distance filter. Published fields cover the active trip, authorization, recording flags, background limitation, and live metrics the UI binds to. Background updates stay off until Always authorization is granted.

sections.title: Attach, auth, and restore
sections.explanation: `attach` supplies the ModelContext used for inserts. Authorization helpers request When-In-Use or escalate to Always. `restoreActiveTripIfNeeded` rehydrates an unfinished vehicle trip into live state, rebuilds `lastAcceptedLocation` from the last point, and resumes updates—blocking if another vehicle still has an active trip.

sections.title: Start, end, and discard
sections.explanation: `start` refuses conflicting active trips, seeds estimated economy from FuelStats averages via TripStats, inserts a new active Trip, resets live counters, and begins location updates. `end` finalizes metrics, deletes near-empty trips unless `keepEmptyTrip`, or marks them completed; `discard` deletes unconditionally. `findPersistedActiveTrip` uses a FetchDescriptor on `statusRaw`.

sections.title: Updates lifecycle helpers
sections.explanation: `beginUpdates` / `stopUpdates` toggle Core Location and the background-limited flag. `clearSession` zeroes live UI state after end/discard. Duration and average speed come from TripStats; `finalizeLiveFields` writes those values plus end coordinates onto the Trip before persistence.

sections.title: Accept points and CL delegates
sections.explanation: `accept` drops inaccurate fixes, re-anchors (without adding distance) on jumps over 200 m, otherwise accumulates distance in the vehicle’s unit and inserts a sequenced TripPoint. Speeds update live max/current. Delegate methods hop back to the main actor to refresh authorization, process batches of locations, or store errors.

Sources/FuelTrack/Services/TripStats.swi.overview: TripStats holds pure geometry and filtering helpers used by TripRecorder in tour step 9. It defines accuracy and jump thresholds, haversine distance, unit conversions for speed/distance, average speed, duration, and the passthrough that snapshots fuel-economy averages onto a trip. Smoke tests exercise these rules without a device.

sections.title: Accuracy and distance math
sections.explanation: Constants require horizontal accuracy between 0 and 50 m and reject jumps beyond 200 m. `haversineMeters` provides an independent great-circle distance; `hasAcceptableAccuracy` and `shouldAccept` encode the recorder’s GPS acceptance policy so tests and production share one definition of a usable fix.

sections.title: Unit speed and economy
sections.explanation: `distanceInUnit` and `speedInUnit` convert SI metres / m/s into the vehicle’s miles or kilometres via `OdometerUnit`. Average speed divides distance by hours of duration. `estimatedEconomy` intentionally just forwards FuelStats averages—trip “MPG” is an estimate from the fuel log, not GPS fuel burn.

Sources/FuelTrack/Views/Trips/HomeTripCa.overview: HomeTripCard is the dashboard entry point for the GPS trip logger in tour step 9. It attaches TripRecorder, restores an active trip for the current vehicle, and either offers Start trip or shows live distance/speed/MPG with Open and End controls. Starting a trip seeds economy from FuelStats averages.

sections.title: Card shell and inactive CTA
sections.explanation: The card observes TripRecorder and detects whether this vehicle owns the active trip. Idle state shows a short explanation and Start; active state swaps in `liveBlock`. On appear and vehicle change it attaches the ModelContext and restores any persisted active trip. Sheets and a confirmation dialog open ActiveTripView or end/discard.

sections.title: Live metrics and start
sections.explanation: `liveBlock` warns when only When-In-Use is granted, shows Formatters-backed chips for distance, speed, average, and estimated MPG, and offers Open, End, and Settings deep-link when Always is missing. `start` computes FuelStats for the vehicle, passes averages into TripRecorder, and presents ActiveTripView on success.

Sources/FuelTrack/Services/FuelioCSVExpo.overview: FuelioCSVExporter writes a vehicle’s SwiftData graph back out as a multi-section Fuelio-compatible CSV—the export half of tour step 10. It emits Vehicle, Log, CostCategories, Costs, and FavStations sections with quoted fields so users can round-trip data toward Fuelio or another FuelTrack import.

sections.title: Vehicle and fill-up log
sections.explanation: `export` builds the Vehicle section with Fuelio DistUnit/FuelUnit codes (miles vs km, litres) and tank type from `fuelType.fuelioTankCode`. The Log section walks `sortedFillUps`, writing date, odometer, liters, full/missed flags, total price, coordinates, station, notes, and StationID—mirroring the columns the importer expects.

sections.title: Costs and favourite stations
sections.explanation: CostCategories enumerates the app’s `CostCategory` cases with stable IDs; Costs maps each car cost’s category key to those IDs and fills Fuelio’s wider column set with empty placeholders where FuelTrack has no equivalent. FavStations exports saved places with lat/lon and external IDs, then joins all lines with newlines.

sections.title: CSV escape and dates
sections.explanation: `csv` doubles embedded quotes for RFC4180-style escaping. Dates always use `en_US_POSIX` with `yyyy-MM-dd`, matching the ImportCSVDateFormat advertised in the Vehicle section so the same file round-trips cleanly through FuelioCSVImporter.

Sources/FuelTrack/Services/FuelioCSVImpo.overview: FuelioCSVImporter parses Fuelio multi-section CSV exports into DTOs for vehicles, fill-ups, costs, and favourite stations—tour step 10’s migration bridge. It normalizes distance/fuel units, dates, and tank codes, counts skipped log rows, and exposes a robust quoted-CSV parser. Settings UI maps the result into SwiftData after currency selection.

sections.title: Import DTOs and errors
sections.explanation: `FuelioImportResult` and the Imported* structs are Sendable plain data so parsing stays free of SwiftData. `FuelioImportError` covers empty files, missing Vehicle/Log sections, missing vehicle rows, and encoding failures with user-facing messages that point back to exporting from Fuelio.

sections.title: Top-level parse flow
sections.explanation: `parse` decodes UTF-8 (falling back to Latin-1), extracts Vehicle and Log sections, maps DistUnit and Tank1Type, cleans the registration plate, and can return early with empty fill-ups if the log is header-only. Log rows become ImportedFillUps after unit inference from headers; costs and favourite stations are always parsed from optional sections.

sections.title: Section splitting and CSV rows
sections.explanation: Section helpers find `## Name` markers (quoted or not) and slice until the next marker. `parseCSVRow` implements a minimal quoted-field scanner with doubled-quote escapes so station names and notes with commas survive. Header/row dictionaries make later field lookup resilient to column reordering.

sections.title: Field lookup and fill-up rows
sections.explanation: `value` prefers exact then prefix key matches; `fuelAmountValue` carefully avoids FuelType/FuelUnit columns. Fill-up parsing accepts Date or legacy Data, converts gallons to litres, maps Full/Missed flags, and tries multiple date patterns. `inferFuelUnit` reads log headers so litre-labelled exports win even when FuelUnit is wrong or zero.

sections.title: Fuel type, costs, stations
sections.explanation: `mapFuelType` translates Fuelio tank codes into FuelTrack’s FuelType enum (petrol blends, diesel, LPG, EV, hybrid). Optional CostCategories/Costs/FavStations sections resolve category names by ID and build ImportedCost/ImportedStation arrays, completing the importer’s coverage of the same sections the exporter writes.

Sources/FuelTrack/Views/Settings/FuelioI.overview: Settings UI for migrating a Fuelio CSV export into FuelTrack. It presents currency and active-vehicle options, opens a document picker for CSV/plain text, then calls FuelioCSVImporter and inserts Vehicle, FillUp, CarCost, and SavedStation rows into SwiftData. This is the user-facing half of tour step 10 (Fuelio Import and Export).

sections.title: Environment and import state
sections.explanation: The view pulls `modelContext`, `dismiss`, and `ActiveVehicleStore` from the environment, and reads the app-wide default currency from `@AppStorage`. Local `@State` tracks the file picker, chosen currency, whether to activate the imported vehicle, progress, and success/error copy. Keeping import UI state local keeps the form self-contained while still sharing the global model and active-vehicle services.

sections.title: Form and file picker
sections.explanation: The form explains how to export from Fuelio, lets the user pick a currency and an “set as active” toggle, then triggers `fileImporter` for `.commaSeparatedText`, `.plainText`, or `.data`. On appear, currency is seeded from the stored default. Success and failure paths clear the opposite message so the Result and Error sections stay mutually exclusive.

sections.title: Parse and insert records
sections.explanation: `importFile` security-scopes the picked URL, parses with `FuelioCSVImporter.parse`, then inserts a new `Vehicle` plus fill-ups, car costs, and favourite stations—all stamped with the chosen currency. After `modelContext.save()`, it optionally selects the vehicle via `activeVehicleStore` and builds a pluralized status string that also reports skipped invalid rows. Errors surface as localized descriptions without leaving partial UI state hanging (`isImporting` is cleared in `defer`).

Sources/FuelTrack/Services/FuelTrackBack.overview: Defines the versioned FuelTrackBackup JSON schema and turns live SwiftData graphs into a portable snapshot. Format version 2 includes nested trips and trip points alongside vehicles, personal spend, budgets, and custom categories. Tour step 11 (Native Backup Round-Trip) starts here on the encode side.

sections.title: Format and root snapshot
sections.explanation: `formatName` and `formatVersion` are the contract the importer validates. `Snapshot` is a Codable envelope: format string, version, export timestamp, then arrays for vehicles and personal-finance records. Marking the structs `Sendable` keeps the DTO layer usable across concurrency boundaries without tying them to SwiftData models.

sections.title: VehicleBackup and decoder
sections.explanation: `VehicleBackup` mirrors vehicle identity, DVLA/compliance fields, and nested collections. The custom `init(from:)` is the compatibility hinge: `trips` uses `decodeIfPresent` and defaults to `[]`, so older v1 backups that omit trips still decode. Explicit `CodingKeys` keep encode/decode stable as fields grow.

sections.title: Nested backup DTOs
sections.explanation: Trip, trip-point, fill-up, car-cost, reminder, station, personal-expense, budget, and custom-category structs are plain Codable value types. Enums and SwiftData relationships are flattened to strings, UUIDs, and optional coordinates so the file is self-describing and independent of the live model graph.

sections.title: Snapshot build and file write
sections.explanation: `makeSnapshot` sorts each collection for deterministic output, then `exportJSON` encodes with pretty printing, sorted keys, and ISO-8601 dates. `writeBackupFile` drops an atomically written temp file named with a local timestamp stamp—handy for the share sheet without inventing a permanent on-disk archive location.

sections.title: Model-to-DTO mappers
sections.explanation: Private helpers map each SwiftData type onto its backup DTO, converting enums via `rawValue` and using sorted relationship accessors (`sortedFillUps`, `sortedCosts`, `sortedPoints`). Category keys and trip status stay as strings so restore can rehydrate enums with fallbacks. This keeps export logic centralized and free of view concerns.

Sources/FuelTrack/Services/FuelTrackBack.overview: Parses FuelTrackBackup JSON, validates format/version, and idempotently upserts every record into SwiftData by UUID. It is the restore counterpart to the exporter and powers the Settings backup import flow in tour step 11.

sections.title: Errors and result summary
sections.explanation: `FuelTrackBackupImportError` covers unreadable JSON, wrong format name, and unsupported versions with user-facing copy. `FuelTrackBackupImportResult` tallies inserts/updates across entity kinds and builds a pluralized `summary` string used by the Settings UI after a successful restore.

sections.title: Parse and orchestrate import
sections.explanation: `parse` decodes with ISO-8601 dates, then requires `format == FuelTrackBackup` and a version between 1 and the current exporter version. `importSnapshot` upserts custom categories first, then each vehicle and its children, then personal expenses and budgets, and finally saves once. `importData` is a thin parse-then-import convenience.

sections.title: Upsert vehicle and children
sections.explanation: Each upsert fetches by UUID predicate: existing rows are updated in place; missing rows are inserted with the backup’s id. Vehicle fields (including compliance) are always overwritten from the snapshot. Fill-ups, car costs, reminders, and saved stations follow the same insert-or-update pattern and re-attach the parent vehicle—making re-import safe.

sections.title: Personal finance upserts
sections.explanation: Personal expenses and budgets are top-level (not nested under a vehicle). Expense category is restored via `categoryKey` / enum fallbacks; budgets treat an empty category string as an overall monthly limit. Currency decoding defaults to GBP when raw values are unknown.

sections.title: Trips and custom categories
sections.explanation: Updating a trip deletes existing points before re-inserting the backup’s GPS samples, avoiding duplicate sequences on re-import. New trips are created with status decoded from the stored raw string. Custom categories restore name, SF Symbol, and car/personal scope so SpendCategoryCatalog can resolve them after restore.

Sources/FuelTrack/Views/Settings/BackupI.overview: Settings screen that restores a FuelTrack backup JSON via the document picker. It wires `FuelTrackBackupImporter` into SwiftData and can activate the first restored vehicle—completing the native backup round-trip UI in tour step 11.

sections.title: State and form UI
sections.explanation: Like the Fuelio import screen, this form explains the idempotent-by-ID restore behavior, offers a toggle to activate the first restored vehicle, and uses `fileImporter` limited to JSON/data types. Progress, result, and error sections mirror the Fuelio flow so Settings import experiences stay consistent.

sections.title: Security-scoped restore
sections.explanation: `importFile` accesses the security-scoped URL, parses then imports the snapshot, and optionally selects the first vehicle UUID from the snapshot via a SwiftData fetch. Status text comes from `result.summary`; any thrown importer or I/O error becomes `errorMessage`. `defer` always clears `isImporting` and stops security-scoped access when started.

Sources/FuelTrack/Models/CarCost.swift.overview: SwiftData model for vehicle-linked non-fuel expenses (service, MOT, insurance, and custom categories). It is a core Spend-tab entity in tour step 12 and also appears in Fuelio CSV import and native backups.

sections.title: Stored properties and relationship
sections.explanation: `@Model` persists id, title, date, optional odometer, amount, raw currency/category strings, note, and createdAt, plus an optional `vehicle` relationship. Storing currency and category as raw strings keeps SwiftData schema simple while typed accessors sit above the persistence layer.

sections.title: Init and typed accessors
sections.explanation: The initializer accepts either a built-in `CostCategory` or an explicit `categoryKey` (used for custom catalog keys). `currencyCode` and `category` bridge to enums with `.gbp` / `.other` fallbacks; `categoryKey` exposes the raw string for catalog resolution and backup round-trips without losing custom ids.

Sources/FuelTrack/Models/PersonalExpense.overview: SwiftData models for personal (non-vehicle) spending and monthly budgets. Together with car costs they extend FuelTrack into personal finance for tour step 12 (Spend and Personal Budgets).

sections.title: PersonalExpense model
sections.explanation: `PersonalExpense` stores title, date, amount, currency, category, note, payment method, and createdAt—no vehicle link. Typed `currencyCode` and `category` accessors wrap raw strings; `categoryKey` lets the spend catalog resolve built-in or custom keys the same way car costs do.

sections.title: PersonalBudget model
sections.explanation: `PersonalBudget` holds a monthly limit and currency. An empty `categoryRaw` means an overall budget (`isOverall`); a non-empty value scopes the limit to a `PersonalExpenseCategory`. That empty-string convention is what backup import restores when `category` is blank in JSON.

Sources/FuelTrack/Services/SpendCategory.overview: Resolves built-in and custom spend categories into display metadata for car and personal scopes. Views and summaries use this catalog instead of hard-coding category enums—central to tour step 12.

sections.title: Resolved category type
sections.explanation: `ResolvedSpendCategory` is a lightweight, identifiable DTO with storage id, display name, SF Symbol, and whether it is custom. Separating resolution from SwiftData models lets lists and pickers share one presentation type.

sections.title: Catalog resolve helpers
sections.explanation: Custom keys are namespaced with a `c:` UUID prefix so they never collide with built-in raw values. `builtins` maps `CostCategory` or `PersonalExpenseCategory` by scope; `all` appends sorted custom categories for that scope. `resolve` looks up a key in the combined list and falls back to a synthetic “Other”/raw-key row so orphaned keys still render.

sections.title: Category spend row
sections.explanation: `CategorySpendRow` packages a resolved category with period total, all-time total, and entry count for summary UIs. Keeping aggregation fields on a separate struct leaves the catalog focused on identity and display while lists can still show rollups.

Sources/FuelTrack/Views/Costs/SpendRootV.overview: Root of the Spend tab: a segmented Car/Personal switcher that hosts car-cost and personal-expense lists, plus sheets for add forms, budgets, and custom categories. This is the navigation hub for tour step 12.

sections.title: SpendScope enum
sections.explanation: `SpendScope` is a simple `CaseIterable` picker model with Car and Personal titles. Using a dedicated enum (instead of binding directly to catalog scopes) keeps toolbar and content switching readable at the tab root.

sections.title: Scoped content and toolbar
sections.explanation: The body swaps `CarCostListContent` and `PersonalExpenseListView` with a smooth transition keyed by scope. The principal toolbar is a segmented picker; leading shows a vehicle menu on car scope or budgets on personal; trailing opens categories and the appropriate add sheet. Add car cost is disabled when no active vehicle is resolved.

sections.title: Active vehicle menu
sections.explanation: `vehicleMenu` lists all queried vehicles and selects via `activeVehicleStore`, marking the current vehicle with a checkmark. This keeps car-cost entry scoped to the same active vehicle used elsewhere in the app without burying vehicle selection inside the list content.

rea-target/FUELIO_FEATURE_MAP.md.overview: Parity checklist mapping Fuelio 10.9.4 capabilities to what FuelTrack already mirrors versus what remains. Tour step 13 uses this document alongside smoke scripts to ground verification and roadmap expectations.

sections.title: Source attribution
sections.explanation: The heading states the comparison target (Fuelio 10.9.4) and that the map was derived from static strings/class names in an unpacked APKM. That provenance clarifies these are feature-level observations, not a runtime API contract.

sections.title: Mirrored capabilities
sections.explanation: The “Mirrored in FuelTrack now” list covers dashboard stats, fuel and cost logs, nearby prices, reminders, multi-vehicle, fuel grades, CSV import/export, GBP/INR settings, and GPS trip log. Reading this against the tour shows which code paths (Fuelio import, FuelStats, trips, spend) already close the gap.

sections.title: Not mirrored yet
sections.explanation: Outstanding Fuelio features include CarPlay/Android Auto, receipt scan, widgets, cloud backup, a historical fill-up map, weather on fill-ups, and premium UI. Native on-device JSON backup is separate from the cloud-backup gap called out here.

Scripts/backup-roundtrip-smoke.swift.overview: Standalone Swift script that encodes and decodes a v2 FuelTrackBackup-shaped fixture, asserts nested IDs and trip points survive, and checks v1 vehicles without `trips` decode to an empty array. Part of tour step 13’s device-free verification suite.

sections.title: Mirrored Codable schema
sections.explanation: The script re-declares Snapshot and nested backup structs so it can run with `swift` without linking the app target. Field layouts intentionally match `FuelTrackBackupExporter` so encode/decode failures here flag schema drift early.

sections.title: V1 trips compatibility types
sections.explanation: `VehicleBackupV1` omits `trips` entirely; `VehicleBackupV2Compat` mirrors the app’s custom decoder that defaults missing trips to `[]`. Together they prove older backups remain readable after the v2 trip fields landed.

sections.title: Fixture encode and assertions
sections.explanation: A fixed-epoch fixture includes vehicle, fill-up, cost, reminder, station, trip with two points, personal expense, overall budget, and a custom category. After ISO-8601 round-trip, the script asserts counts and key IDs, then decodes a v1 vehicle and confirms empty trips, and finally sanity-checks rejecting a non-FuelTrack format name.

Scripts/fuelio-import-smoke.swift.overview: Minimal CSV smoke test that parses a Fuelio multi-section export and asserts vehicle name/fuel unit plus 48 valid fill-up rows. Supports tour step 13 verification of Fuelio CSV shape without the full app importer.

sections.title: CSV and section helpers
sections.explanation: `parseCSVRow` handles quoted fields and escaped quotes; `section` finds `## Name` markers and returns non-empty lines until the next section. These helpers approximate how Fuelio’s multi-section CSV is sliced before row mapping.

sections.title: Fixture assertions
sections.explanation: The script loads a path argument or the default sample CSV, asserts Vehicle Name/FuelUnit, checks Log headers include Date and a Fuel volume column, then counts rows with Date, odometer, and litres present. Expecting exactly 48 fill-ups makes regressions in sample data or parsing obvious.

Scripts/fuelstats-smoke.swift.overview: Standalone smoke test that copies FuelStats full-tank segment math and asserts distance, litres, and L/100km for a three-fill fixture. Tour step 13 uses it to verify economy formulas without a device or SwiftData.

sections.title: Units and segment types
sections.explanation: A minimal `OdometerUnit` converts miles to kilometres; `FillUpSnapshot` and `ConsumptionSegment` mirror the fields the real FuelStats engine needs. `litersPer100km` guards against zero distance or litres before computing the rate.

sections.title: Full-tank segment builder
sections.explanation: `segments(from:)` sorts by odometer then date, ignores skipped fills (resetting the open segment), and only closes a consumption window between successive full tanks. Litres and cost between those anchors become one segment—the same full-tank method described in the README and FuelStats service.

sections.title: Numeric assertions
sections.explanation: The fixture is full → partial → full over 300 miles with 45 litres between full tanks. Assertions check a single segment, distance, litres, and L/100km against the miles-to-km conversion, then print PASS with the computed economy figure.

Scripts/tripstats-smoke.swift.overview: Standalone Swift smoke script that mirrors TripStats / TripRecorder GPS helpers without SwiftData or a device. It reimplements haversine distance, duration, average and unit-converted speed, economy passthrough, and jump re-anchor rules, then asserts them against a short London lat/lon sample pair. Tour step 13 (Smoke Tests and Parity) uses this script as the verification path for GPS trip math called out in the README.

sections.title: Script entry and imports
sections.explanation: The shebang runs the file with `swift` directly from the shell, matching the README verification style for Scripts/*.swift. Only Foundation is imported so Date math and assertions work without linking the FuelTrack package or iOS frameworks.

sections.title: Odometer unit conversion
sections.explanation: A local `OdometerUnit` enum duplicates the app concept of miles vs kilometres for smoke isolation. `fromKilometers` divides by 1.609344 for miles and leaves kilometres unchanged, so later distance and speed checks can exercise the same conversion path the UI uses without importing Models.

sections.title: GPS sample model
sections.explanation: `Sample` is a lightweight stand-in for `TripPoint`: latitude, longitude, timestamp, and optional speed in metres per second. Keeping it a plain struct lets the script build synthetic tracks inline without SwiftData models.

sections.title: Haversine path distance
sections.explanation: `haversineMeters` computes great-circle distance between two WGS84 points using Earth radius 6,371,000 m. `distanceMeters` walks consecutive samples and sums those segments, returning 0 when fewer than two points exist—the same geometry TripStats uses for trip length.

sections.title: Duration and average speed
sections.explanation: `durationSeconds` spans from the first sample to an optional `endedAt`, otherwise the last sample time, clamped at zero. `averageSpeed` divides distance by hours (`durationSeconds / 3600`) and returns 0 when duration is non-positive, avoiding divide-by-zero on empty or instantaneous trips.

sections.title: Speed units and economy
sections.explanation: `speedInUnit` converts m/s to km/h (`* 3.6`) then through `OdometerUnit.fromKilometers` so max speed can be asserted in mph or km/h. `estimatedEconomy` simply echoes average MPG and L/100 values—documenting that trip economy display is a passthrough of vehicle averages rather than deriving from the GPS path here.

sections.title: Jump re-anchor rules
sections.explanation: Constants match TripRecorder: accept fixes with horizontal accuracy ≤ 50 m, and treat jumps over 200 m as GPS glitches. `shouldReAnchorWithoutDistance` returns true only when accuracy is good and the jump exceeds the max—mirroring the production rule that re-anchors the track without adding bogus segment distance.

sections.title: Assertions and PASS output
sections.explanation: Two samples ~1.11 km north of central London over 600 seconds drive the checks: path metres in (1000, 1200), duration ≈ 600 s, positive average speed in miles, max speed matching 20 m/s converted to mph, economy tuple identity, and the three re-anchor cases (large accurate jump yes; small jump no; large inaccurate jump no). Success prints a one-line PASS summary with metres and average mph.
